recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for core reconciliation. No core follow-up is indicated unless Permission is restored to core; future Permission action binding changes should be made in the Data Access Policies IG if that external source of truth changes.
issue_request: Applied/Persuasive Security WG change request asking that Permission.rule.activity.action use the CRUDE-oriented http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/type-restful-interaction value set with preferred binding strength instead of the privacy/consent action vocabulary.
initial_application: Core commit 61227667280962bc6ddbfa74556a90db70d8be9a changed source/permission/structuredefinition-Permission.xml from an example binding to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/consent-action to a preferred binding to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/type-restful-interaction, and that implementation was merged through HL7/fhir#3296.
additional_context: Later commit 0e2a8a7f839d5e1a43787523daccf07d958362f3 removed the Permission resource from core, including source/permission and active source/fhir.ini registrations. The current Security module links Permission to the Data Access Policies IG, whose current source has Permission.rule.activity.action bound with preferred strength to type-restful-interaction. FHIR-49031 was approved and implemented in the same Permission change family and is already represented by an external-repo audit on the combined branch.
reconciliation: Published an empty external-repo audit commit on the combined branch. No core source change was made because the current core checkout no longer owns or builds Permission, and the external Permission source already carries the requested FHIR-49030 binding.
